title: Coinbase CTO says he's getting 'the best feedback' of his career from an AI agent
excerpt: In an era hyper-focused on results, continuous feedback from AI coaches may be the next iteration in optimizing performance.
content_html:
By Ana Altchek

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

No one wants to hear from a colleague that they monopolized a meeting or failed to get their point across — and few colleagues want to be the one to share that with their boss.

While thoughtful feedback can be valuable, it's not always welcome when it's unsolicited. Nowadays, Coinbase CTO Rob Witoff is getting that kind of candid advice regularly from a source he doesn't have to worry about awkward workplace dynamics with: an AI agent.

"That's the kind of feedback I'm getting every single day now," Witoff told Business Insider.

The company recently rolled out a beta version of "Coinbase Coach," an internal AI tool that's been embedded across data sources that workers have access to, including Google Docs, meeting transcripts, Github commits, and Slack messages. It provides employees with private feedback based on interactions with people throughout the company. The reports aren't used in performance reviews or available to managers, Witoff said.

Employees can opt in for the tool while it's in beta, and the tool can review those transcripts alongside their Slack interactions and activity across other internal tools to provide weekly feedback, the CTO said.

When Coinbase linked its internal AI models to company data sources, employees across the organization began building their own agents to automate tasks and get feedback on their work. That experimentation helped inspire Coinbase Coach. The company built an early version in March for a small testing group before rolling out the beta internally in June.

Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong talked about his own personal usage of the tooling in an episode of the "All-In Podcast" in January. He said he used the AI assistant through what he calls "reverse prompting." Rather than giving the model a task, he asks it what he should do based on the data it's gathered throughout the company. It might, for example, flag a disagreement within a team over strategy.

Armstrong said he also asked the model questions about what he's changed his mind about most, or how he could become a better CEO. In response, the model might analyze how the CEO spent his time over the previous quarter and compare that with how he'd intended to spend it.

Pushing for peak performance

In an era hyper-focused on results, continuous feedback from AI coaches may be the next iteration in improving performance.

Witoff said the tool is part of a broader effort for the company to rethink what it means to improve efficiency.

"We are moving toward a culture of proactive coaching," Witoff said.

The cryptocurrency platform laid off 14% of its staff, roughly 700 workers, in May, eliminating "pure managers" as it shifts toward smaller teams and leans more on individual contributors. On some teams, a single employee may serve as engineer, designer, and product manager.

Witoff said he's getting some of the best advice of his career because he has an impartial agent who isn't afraid to tell him the hard things.

"Not so I can be micromanaged," Witoff said. "So I can get good feedback to be the best version of myself I can be."

Witoff said the feedback tends to center on two themes. One is communication: The coach will tell him when he isn't being as direct or clear as he could be, prompting him to sharpen his point, communicate it more efficiently, or articulate a clearer strategy.

The other is knowing when to step back. Witoff said he can sometimes get too tactical, prompting the coach to tell him he's "too in the weeds" and should focus more on strategy while leaving execution to others.

作者：Ana Altchek 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

没有人愿意听到同事说他们垄断了一次会议或未能表达自己的观点，也很少有同事愿意与老板分享这些信息。

虽然深思熟虑的反馈可能很有价值，但主动提供的反馈并不总是受欢迎。 如今，Coinbase 首席技术官 Rob Witoff 定期从一个来源获得这种坦诚的建议，他不必担心与人工智能代理的尴尬工作场所关系。

“这就是我现在每天收到的反馈，”维托夫告诉《商业内幕》。

该公司最近推出了“Coinbase Coach”的测试版，这是一种内部人工智能工具，已嵌入员工可以访问的数据源中，包括 Google 文档、会议记录、Github 提交和 Slack 消息。 它根据与整个公司人员的互动为员工提供私人反馈。 维托夫说，这些报告不会用于​​绩效评估，也不会提供给经理。

首席技术官表示，员工可以在该工具处于测试阶段时选择使用该工具，该工具可以审查这些记录以及他们在其他内部工具中的 Slack 交互和活动，以提供每周反馈。

当 Coinbase 将其内部人工智能模型连接到公司数据源时，整个组织的员工开始构建自己的代理来自动化任务并获取工作反馈。 这一实验激发了 Coinbase Coach 的灵感。 该公司于 3 月份为一个小型测试小组构建了一个早期版本，然后于 6 月份在内部推出了测试版。

Coinbase 首席执行官布莱恩·阿姆斯特朗 (Brian Armstrong) 在一月份的“All-In Podcast”节目中谈到了他个人对该工具的使用。 他说他通过他所谓的“反向提示”来使用人工智能助手。 他没有给模型分配任务，而是根据在整个公司收集的数据询问模型应该做什么。 例如，它可能会标记团队内部对策略的分歧。

阿姆斯特朗表示，他还向模特询问了他在哪些方面改变最多的想法，或者他如何才能成为一名更好的首席执行官。 作为回应，该模型可能会分析首席执行官在上一季度如何度过时间，并将其与他打算如何度过时间进行比较。

推动巅峰表现

在一个高度关注结果的时代，人工智能教练的持续反馈可能是提高绩效的下一个迭代。

维托夫表示，该工具是该公司重新思考提高效率的更广泛努力的一部分。

“我们正在走向积极主动的辅导文化，”维托夫说。

该加密货币平台在 5 月份解雇了 14% 的员工，大约 700 名员工，随着它转向更小的团队并更多地依赖个人贡献者，消除了“纯粹的管理者”。 在某些团队中，一名员工可能担任工程师、设计师和产品经理。

维托夫说，他得到了职业生涯中一些最好的建议，因为他有一位公正的经纪人，他不怕告诉他困难的事情。

“不是这样，我就可以被微观管理，”维托夫说。 “这样我就可以获得良好的反馈，成为最好的自己。”

维托夫表示，反馈往往集中在两个主题上。 一是沟通：当他表达得不够直接或清晰时，教练会告诉他，促使他阐明自己的观点，更有效地沟通，或者阐明更清晰的策略。

另一个是知道何时退一步。 维托夫说，他有时会过于战术化，这促使教练告诉他，他“太过于草率”，应该更多地关注战略，而将执行留给其他人。
